title: EU launches network to harness health data and AI for cardiovascular care
key_facts: The European Cardiovascular Health Data and AI Network (CHAIN) has been launched with EU4Health funding.
It is a 36-month project coordinated by the European Society of Cardiology (ESC).
A consortium of 53 partners from 20 European countries takes part, including universities, hospitals, technology companies, health ministries and patient groups.
It builds on the ESC's EuroHeart registry network covering 18 countries.
Six real-world use cases will run across 13 countries, covering prevention, early detection and decision support.
Validated AI tools will be listed in a European repository with 'AI Passports' documenting performance, safety and suitability.
The text says cardiovascular disease causes one in three deaths in Europe and costs the EU €282 billion.
quote_evidence: The question is no longer simply what AI can do. The question is how we make it work safely and effectively for patients and health professionals in everyday healthcare.
why_it_matters_hint: A European network aims to test and validate cardiology AI across hospitals so trusted tools can reach patients.
